pages.quiz:
WOODWORK — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #20
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: WOODWORK
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When learning Manufactured boards, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Manufactured boards.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Manufactured boards.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Manufactured boards.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Manufactured boards.

2. When learning Mass Production, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Mass Production.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Mass Production.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Mass Production.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Mass Production.

3. When learning Finishing, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Finishing.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Finishing.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Finishing.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Finishing.

4. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. Input Cable Tester
   B. Information and Communication Technology
   C. Internal Cooking Timer
   D. International Cricket Team

5. When learning Portable Power Tools, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Portable Power Tools.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Portable Power Tools.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Portable Power Tools.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Portable Power Tools.

6. When learning Detailed drawing, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Detailed drawing.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Detailed drawing.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Detailed drawing.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Detailed drawing.

7. When learning Orthographic Drawing, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Orthographic Drawing.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Orthographic Drawing.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Orthographic Drawing.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Orthographic Drawing.

8. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Remove all guards
   B. Work alone with eyes closed
   C. Wear safety gear and follow instructions
   D. Run with the tool

9. When learning Health and Safety in the Workshop, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Health and Safety in the Workshop.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Health and Safety in the Workshop.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Health and Safety in the Workshop.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Health and Safety in the Workshop.

10. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Overload every socket
   B. Never touch live wires with wet hands
   C. Ignore burnt cables
   D. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun

11. When learning Project activity, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Project activity.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Project activity.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Project activity.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Project activity.

12. When learning Woodworking Machines, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Woodworking Machines.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Woodworking Machines.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Woodworking Machines.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Woodworking Machines.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Detailed drawing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Trends in woodwork and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Health and Safety in the Workshop and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Portable Power Tools and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Manufactured boards.

2. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Mass Production.

3. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Finishing.

4. B — Information and Communication Technology

5. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Portable Power Tools.

6. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Detailed drawing.

7. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Orthographic Drawing.

8. C — Wear safety gear and follow instructions

9. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Health and Safety in the Workshop.

10. B — Never touch live wires with wet hands

11. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Project activity.

12. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Woodworking Machines.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Detailed drawing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Trends in woodwork; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Health and Safety in the Workshop; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Portable Power Tools; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
